# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 9 (Bu-Vb Np9)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Np9
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 9
**Title (English, from literature):** Requesting a fine robe from a combined fund
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bu-vb-np9
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin01m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
*Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 9* (also titled *Dutiyaupakkhata*) is the ninth training rule in the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* chapter of the Theravāda *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* [SuttaCentral]. The rule addresses the situation where two separate lay donors each set aside robe funds to purchase robes for a monk. If the monk approaches them without prior invitation and asks them to combine their funds to buy him a single fine robe, he commits an offense requiring forfeiture (*nissaggiya*) of the acquired robe and confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
The rule corresponds to the ninth rule of the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* division in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Bhikkhu Parivāra*, with an equivalent counterpart in the nun's discipline (*Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 19*) [SuttaCentral]. It is widely preserved across early Buddhist monastic lineages, having full parallels in the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Lokottaravāda Vinayas in Chinese, Tibetan, Sanskrit, and Gāndhārī [SuttaCentral]. Computational analysis by DharmaNexus reflects extensive Pali-internal text reuse with structurally similar robe-procurement rules, particularly *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 8* and *27*, as well as alignments with canonical and paracanonical Tibetan Vinaya treatises such as the *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-2) and the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
